short: TWIST1/2, HAND1/2, TCF21, SCX and MESP1/2 are class II basic helix-loop-helix factors of mesoderm and neural crest. They bind the E-box CANNTG as heterodimers with the ubiquitous E-proteins TCF3/TCF4/TCF12, with each other, or as homodimers, and this group prefers CAGATG (CATCTG on the opposite strand). Because the two central E-box bases are barely contacted by the protein, the distinction from the muscle E-box CAGCTG and the neural CATATG is weak. TWIST has one genuinely diagnostic feature: a double E-box with the two boxes five bases apart, which aligns two TWIST-E47 dimers on one face of the helix so they can tetramerise. The family runs craniofacial, cardiac, tendon and epithelial-mesenchymal transition programmes.
long:
## The factors

TWIST1, TWIST2 (DERMO-1), HAND1 (eHAND/Thing1), HAND2 (dHAND/Thing2), TCF21 (capsulin/epicardin/POD1), SCX (scleraxis) and MESP1/MESP2 make up this family. All are class II bHLH proteins of mesodermal and neural-crest lineages, and all bind DNA as dimers: heterodimers with the ubiquitous class I E-proteins TCF3, TCF4 and TCF12, homodimers, and heterodimers with each other. The TWIST1-HAND2 pairing matters functionally, because different dimer species have different activities and the balance between them is set post-translationally. Phosphorylation of two conserved residues in helix I by protein kinase A and protein kinase C, reversed by protein phosphatase 2A, shifts TWIST1 and HAND2 dimer choice, and mutations that alter that balance produce limb and craniofacial phenotypes overlapping the TWIST1 loss-of-function syndrome. TWIST1 additionally carries a C-terminal WR ("Twist-box") domain that dimerises, allowing two TWIST1-E47 dimers to assemble into a tetramer. Expression is lineage-restricted but broad within those lineages: TWIST1/2 in cranial and limb mesenchyme, dermis and many mesenchymal tumours; HAND1 in extraembryonic mesoderm, left ventricle and trophoblast; HAND2 in right ventricle, branchial arches and sympathoadrenal cells; TCF21 in epicardium, kidney, lung mesenchyme and vascular smooth muscle; SCX in tendon; MESP1/2 in nascent mesoderm.

## The motif

The core is again a six-base E-box, CANNTG, with each monomer reading one CAN half-site. This family's preference is written CAGATG, or equivalently CATCTG read on the other strand, and that is what the data give: the representative model is `CCAGATGT` (CIS-BP TWIST1 and JASPAR TWIST1 MA1123.3 agree exactly), with HOCOMOCO TWIST1 ChIP models reading ACATCTG. The distinction from the muscle E-box CAGCTG and the neural CAGATG/CATATG is weak by construction — the two central bases are the ones that vary, and in the one solved class I/class II structure on an asymmetric E-box (E47-NEUROD1 on CATCTG) no side chain contacts the central base pairs directly. Expect substantial cross-matching.

The one feature in this family with real discriminating power is architectural rather than compositional. High-resolution mapping of TWIST occupancy in human and *Drosophila* genomes found that TWIST, and not other bHLH proteins tested, prefers a double E-box with the two boxes separated by five nucleotides; the spacing aligns two TWIST-E47 dimers on the same face of the helix so that the WR domains can contact each other and form a stable tetramer. The data carry that signature: `TWST2.H14CORE.0.P.B` reads CAGCTGGNNNCCAGATGT, two E-boxes five bases apart, in a single model.

Cohesion here is the lowest of the E-box families at 0.76, and label agreement is poor for most members. TCF21 has one high-grade model reading AACAGCTGG (a myogenic-type site) and another reading CATATGGT (a NeuroD/Atonal-type site). MESP1/MESP2 models read CATATG or CACCTG. The HAND models are the weakest: `HAND1.H14CORE.0.P.B` and `HAND2.H14CORE.0.P.B` are nearly identical to one another (TCTGGNTTNTGTCA) but resemble nothing else, and JASPAR's Hand1 MA2123.1 (CCAGACCT) and Hand1::Tcf3 MA0092.2 (GTCTGGCA) are not recognisable E-boxes at all, while the one HT-SELEX HAND2 model reads GCACCTGC. Three mutually inconsistent HAND2 models exist across the four databases.

## Where it acts

These are enhancer factors in mesenchymal, cardiac and neural-crest chromatin, not CpG-island promoter factors. TWIST1 sites occur in epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) programmes alongside SNAI, ZEB, TEAD and AP-1 motifs; the double E-box is the TWIST-specific arrangement. HAND2 sites sit in the core regulatory circuitry of the adrenergic/noradrenergic state of neuroblastoma, co-occurring with PHOX2B, GATA3, ASCL1 and TBX2 motifs in large super-enhancer clusters, and the same circuit can switch to a mesenchymal state with an entirely different motif complement. TCF21 acts in smooth-muscle and fibroblast enhancers; the coronary artery disease association at 6q23.2 maps to an enhancer regulating *TCF21* expression rather than to coding variation.

## Biology and disease

TWIST1 haploinsufficiency causes Saethre-Chotzen syndrome, with coronal craniosynostosis, facial asymmetry and limb anomalies; both founding reports identified loss-of-function and missense changes clustered in the bHLH domain. TWIST1 is also required for EMT-associated metastasis in mammary tumour models. *Hand1*-null mouse embryos die with extraembryonic and cardiac defects; *Hand2* (dHAND) loss disrupts right ventricle and branchial-arch development and sympathetic neuron differentiation. *Mesp1* is expressed in heart precursors and required for a single heart tube. HAND2 is a dependency of adrenergic neuroblastoma. TCF21 variation contributes to coronary artery disease risk through smooth-muscle phenotype.

## Reading a hit

A CAGATG or CATCTG match says a class II bHLH-E-protein dimer of this general kind could bind. It does not tell you which factor, and the separation from the NEUROD/ATOH family (CAGATG/CATATG) and the MYOD family (CAGCTG) is one or two bases at positions the protein barely touches. If you want evidence that a site is genuinely TWIST-type rather than generically bHLH, look for the double E-box with a five-base spacer; a single E-box will not settle it. Treat HAND1 and HAND2 models with particular caution: all of the HAND ChIP-derived models in this family are HOCOMOCO grade B with `P` (ChIP-only) evidence, they do not look like E-boxes, and they match nothing else in the collection, which is the expected signature of an indirect or low-quality model rather than of a HAND recognition sequence. One CIS-BP TWIST2 model is inherited from the mouse protein at 100% DBD identity, which is harmless. Because the family's own members disagree about their preferred site, do not use a hit to assign a specific paralogue.
caveats: This is the least cohesive of the E-box families in the atlas (cohesion 0.76), and its members disagree with each other. TCF21 has one high-grade model reading a myogenic AACAGCTGG and another reading a NeuroD-type CATATGGT; HAND2 has three mutually inconsistent models across the four databases. The HAND1 and HAND2 models from ChIP are nearly identical to one another, are not recognisable E-boxes, and resemble nothing else in the collection — treat them as unreliable rather than as HAND recognition sequences. A single CAGATG or CATCTG hit identifies the general class II bHLH site, not the factor. Only the five-base-spaced double E-box discriminates TWIST specifically.
